transport.bind_policy: localhost or explicit IPv4 loopback only
transport.health: GET /healthz is anonymous and returns service/version only
transport.readiness: api serve prints one JSON line with the actual bound port; --port 0 is supported

authentication.internal_api: no application credential; this transport is trusted local infrastructure
authentication.bind_policy: the API binds only to exact loopback and rejects non-loopback Host or Origin values
authentication.browser_policy: browser JavaScript never calls this internal port directly; the public Console session and project upstream credentials remain separate boundaries

request_rules.mutations: agent and canonical project attribution are required
request_rules.port_release: lease_id or port plus acting agent and owning project
request_rules.server_launch: structured argv is preferred; legacy cmd is parsed without a shell and rejects shell operators
request_rules.exact_lease_start: lease_id requires structured argv and an active unbound manual lease owned by the same agent/project
request_rules.docker: real commands resolve an absolute Docker entry point and are bounded by observation/lifecycle timeouts
request_rules.durable_lifecycle: target_kind is project, server, container, volume, or worktree; repository is accepted only as compatibility input and is normalized to project; exact volume purge requires fresh complete Compose ownership plus zero native container references; archive/purge always require a fresh plan and apply is bound to plan_id plus plan_fingerprint; restore is an explicit owner-invoked endpoint

event_contract.observe: POST /v1/observe accepts exactly {agent,project} and commits one explicit full-Docker host observation; repeated unchanged samples append no transition events and unavailable or unobservable capabilities never invent stopped resources
event_contract.read: GET /v1/events returns schema_version, events, next_cursor, and has_more in durable insertion-sequence order; after is the opaque high-watermark cursor from the prior page and limit is 1 through 500. occurred_at is event information, not the pagination key, so a slow operation committed later cannot fall behind the cursor merely because its event time is earlier
event_contract.privacy: diagnostic_json and other private operation evidence are never returned by the event feed
event_contract.catch_up: persist next_cursor only after the consumer durably handles every returned event; when has_more is true, request the next page immediately before polling again

state.read_model: GET /v1/state is a compatibility control snapshot derived from normalized SQLite; it is not the authoritative persistence format
state.persistence: server-wide service-owned 0700 authority directory and 0600 coordinator.sqlite3; trusted local clients use the Unix broker and retain only private execution journals
state.durable_ports: successful server start/register pins project+name to a port until explicit unassign or attributed state reset
state.operations: short reservation/commit lock phases with same-target exclusion and bounded journal evidence

inventory_contract.ordinary_inventory: GET /v1/inventory returns the single server-wide broker snapshot without runtime sampling or persistence, including services configured from any local repository
inventory_contract.compatibility_policy: legacy Console rows are nested under v1_compatibility; non-colliding legacy aliases may also appear at top level, but top-level leases and port_assignments always retain normalized lease_id/assignment_id and repo_id identities
inventory_contract.no_docker: GET /v1/inventory/no-docker returns the committed normalized snapshot without a Docker CLI/daemon probe; when the systemd readiness client supplies exactly one project, name, and port query target, only compatibility rows that can affect that registration graph receive bounded current process, listener, and health observation on an in-memory copy; the route excludes unrelated services, process-usage sampling, and backup discovery and never persists derived lifecycle or lease changes
inventory_contract.project_usage: rows include stable usage_key plus authoritative server_ids and exact container_resource_ids; container_names remain legacy display data and are not ownership keys
inventory_contract.agent_browsers: an optional schema-1, path-free sidecar projection reports measured non-project headless/automation browser sessions, last observed resource work, bounded cleanup history, and idle-reaper policy. Project/container browser trees are excluded to avoid double accounting; omission leaves their bytes honestly in System / unclassified and never invalidates repository inventory
inventory_contract.docker_association: Compose labels and verified coordinator sidecars provide exact repository association; name similarity is read-only evidence and is never used as a mutation target
inventory_contract.project_reports: ok=false must be treated as failure even when HTTP status is 200; inspect partial, preflight_failed, classification, actions, and action_errors

test_contract.repositories: GET /v1/test-repositories returns every current protected-profile repository ID and display name joined to testd's retained ready, missing, or invalid setup projection; the response never scans user worktrees and never exposes canonical paths, manifest text, argv, environment values, or fixture secrets
test_contract.setup: GET /v1/test-repositories/:repo_id/setup executes the bounded repository-UID setup projection and returns only ready, missing, or invalid plus sanitized graph, policy, fixture, network, isolation, and input-coverage facts; it never returns argv, environment values, absolute repository paths, or manifest text
test_contract.read: GET /v1/tests requires one configured repo_id plus optional days (1-3650) and limit (1-500), and serves summary, comparison, daily and hourly data from testd-owned materialized TestDB rollups rather than legacy authority test tables
test_contract.fleet: GET /v1/test-fleet accepts hours (1-168, default 24) and returns one bounded projection from testd-owned materialized TestDB rollups, scoped to the caller's exact current repository enrollments and keyed only by immutable repo_id: sparse repository-by-hour exact test seconds, capacity, health, efficiency, queue wait, freshness and actionable repository attention. Test assertion/error failures and infrastructure/setup failures have separate state, count, rate and detail fields. Repository state_scope is selected_window: it describes observations in the requested window and does not claim a historical failure remains unresolved. The read never accesses legacy authority test records or returns paths, commands, logs, or case identities
test_contract.plan: POST /v1/test-plan accepts repo_id, intent, one caller-generated canonical operation_id UUID, one exact schema-1 source selector, and an optional bounded requested_targets list for manual intent only. Original and temporary selectors carry an immutable repository ID plus catalog generation; temporary canonical paths are resolved only from the installed broker profile and revalidated by the broker. The returned plan preserves operation_id so retries are durably idempotent. Target names must come from the sanitized configured-repository setup catalog; dependency closure, manifest, argv, resources and policy remain derived inside the test plane
test_contract.submit: POST /v1/test-runs accepts repo_id, plan_id and operation_id plus the trusted API's bounded diagnostic actor; the canonical UUID is the durable idempotency key, and the plan must resolve to the same immutable repository before mutation
test_contract.history: GET /v1/test-runs requires repo_id and accepts one opaque after cursor, one state filter, and limit 1-200; results are repository-scoped and do not expose another repository's run existence
test_contract.run_reads: GET /v1/test-runs/:run_id and /summary return bounded run status and the <=8 KiB agent summary. /failures, /artifacts and /cases use cursor pagination with a maximum page of 50 and are reauthorized against the run's immutable repository before any result is disclosed
test_contract.events: GET /v1/test-events requires repo_id and accepts a non-negative numeric event cursor plus limit 1-500; events are repository-scoped and polling never clears retained Console content
test_contract.control: POST /v1/test-runs/:run_id/cancel accepts reason and operation_id. POST /retry accepts failed_only and operation_id. Every mutation is idempotent, reauthorizes the actual run repository, and does not trust the run ID as an ownership claim
test_contract.google_authorization: Google sign-in protects the Console as a whole. Every signed-in Console user can read, run, cancel, and retry tests for every configured repository; no repository grants, memberships, or owner-only release gate exist. Repository-scoped routes still verify returned target identity for correctness
test_contract.hourly: the read returns seven complete UTC days of hourly buckets; exact case intervals are split at hour boundaries and parallel intervals add, so test_seconds may exceed 3600 in one wall-clock hour; failure_count is attributed to the case start hour
test_contract.comparison: comparison_summary and previous_daily cover the immediately preceding equal period, while dynamics reports suite-level current_seconds, previous_seconds, change_percent, failures, and last_run
test_contract.ownership: the service-owned broker database stores repository-attributed sessions, group runs, and exact individual case timings; clients never receive a database handle
test_contract.inventory: server-wide normalized inventory includes a bounded 30-day test_statistics projection per active repository for DevOps Board
test_contract.privacy: run records retain command fingerprints and selectors, never raw child output, commands, environment values, credentials, or failure payloads

lifecycle_contract.archives: GET /v1/archives returns {archives:[...]}; rows carry target_kind, target_id, display_name, archived_at, reason, actor and may include project_id/parent, restorable, removable, status, retained, effects, and blockers
lifecycle_contract.plan: POST /v1/lifecycle/plan accepts exactly {target_kind,target_id,action:'archive'|'purge',reason}; the response binds plan_id and plan_fingerprint (fingerprint is a compatibility alias) to target/effects/retained/deleted/blockers and supplies the exact purge confirmation_phrase
lifecycle_contract.apply: POST /v1/lifecycle/apply accepts exactly {plan_id,plan_fingerprint,confirmation_phrase}; confirmation_phrase is the empty string for archive and the exact server-issued phrase for purge
lifecycle_contract.restore: POST /v1/lifecycle/restore accepts exactly {target_kind,target_id,reason}; restore clears the durable fence and never implies that the resource started
lifecycle_contract.result_truth: apply and restore return ok, status, partial, needs_attention, and errors; ok=false, partial=true, needs_attention=true, or blocked/failed/partial status is failure even with HTTP 200
lifecycle_contract.retention: archive stops and fences the exact resource while retaining declared data/history; permanent removal is available only for an archived row that advertises removable=true; worktree removal is shown only as an advertised removable child of an archived project

errors.400: invalid request, ownership mismatch, capability failure, or refused mutation
errors.403: a non-loopback Origin is rejected by the trusted local boundary
errors.409: fresh lifecycle evidence blocks the action, the archived capability is unavailable, or an apply/restore result is incomplete
errors.415: POST content type is not application/json
